sources.title: The Formation of False Memories
sources.why_it_matters: Planted a wholly fabricated childhood memory of being lost in a shopping mall at age 5 in 24 adults; 25% recalled the non-existent event with rich invented sensory details.

sources.title: Reconstruction of automobile destruction: An example of the interaction between language and memory
sources.journal: Journal of Verbal Learning and Verbal Behavior
sources.why_it_matters: Showed changing one verb ('smashed' vs 'contacted') after car-crash films raised speed estimates from 31.8 to 40.8 mph and doubled false memories of broken glass.

sources.title: Semantic representations in the temporal pole predict false memories
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
sources.why_it_matters: Demonstrated via human fMRI multivoxel pattern analysis that semantic overlap in the anterior temporal lobe predicts which false memories the brain will endorse as real.

sources.title: False memories, false preferences: Flexible retrieval mechanisms supporting successful inference bias novel decisions.
sources.why_it_matters: Proved that the hippocampus's adaptive flexible retrieval mechanism stitches separate real details together, producing confident false memories as a byproduct.

sources.title: Creating Memories for False Autobiographical Events in Childhood: A Systematic Review
sources.why_it_matters: Critically distinguished partial vs complete autobiographical false-memory endorsement (~15% full memory vs ~25-30% partial/full) across implantation studies.

sources.title: Creating a False Memory in the Hippocampus
sources.why_it_matters: Landmark optogenetic hippocampal engram study proving reactivating a neutral context memory during fear physically writes a false associative memory trace.
